findings.Quote: His neck aches before he registers he's been holding it back to look. He didn't decide to.
findings.Note: Slightly overwrought physical-tell construction for 'he was staring upward a long time' — borders on telling via manufactured physical symptom rather than earned sensation.
findings.Fix: Simplify: 'His neck aches. He's been staring straight up without meaning to.'

findings.Quote: The invoice was the meaning: what the work was, what it cost to run, what she expected back, every field weighted and the blank fields weighted too.
findings.Note: This still frames her communication as fundamentally transactional/document-based, which cuts against the beat's stated purpose of showing she has abandoned transactional framing — the prose argues she's still 'speaking invoice,' just with a gap in it, rather than showing a genuine shift to shared purpose.
findings.Fix: Lean harder into the absence as departure: emphasize that no invoice-logic applies at all, rather than reading the blank as still governed by her fee-language grammar.

findings.Quote: He'd kept at it because the work was right.
findings.Note: Aphoristic filler that tells us the moral rather than demonstrating it; breaks from the beat's otherwise concrete, evidentiary style.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or replace with a specific action Tadesse took.

findings.Quote: He held both versions open at once and felt the floor go out from under the easy assumption that she was simply adding to what he knew.
findings.Note: Tells the reader the magnitude of the realization ('felt the floor go out') instead of letting the contradictory data carry it — a stock destabilization phrase.
findings.Fix: Cut 'felt the floor go out from under' and let the factual contradiction (company record vs. her entry) do the work.

findings.Quote: let the city come up around him the way water comes up when you go under — the pressure of it, the change in temperature, the air doing something the glass had never let it do
findings.Note: drowning/submersion-as-sensory-immersion is a well-worn metaphor and slightly undercuts the literal claim, since city air pressure doesn't behave like water pressure
findings.Fix: anchor the simile in a more specific, literal sensory detail unique to this street rather than the generic underwater image

findings.Quote: the way the lobby downstairs had been waiting on him for eleven years, from the wrong end, without either of them knowing it
findings.Note: strained personification/purple metaphor that doesn't hold up literally — a lobby cannot wait 'from the wrong end,' and the claim is asserted rather than earned
findings.Fix: cut the clause or replace with a concrete image tying lobby and rate field without the personification

findings.Quote: Something left unanswered doesn't sit quiet in him — it stays awake at the back of the skull, low and steady, and won't let him be until someone closes it.
findings.Note: Generic interiority statement telling us his psychology in abstract, aphoristic terms rather than showing it through specific behavior — reads as filler explanation rather than earned insight.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete physical detail specific to Elias (e.g., a habit tied to his procedural nature).

findings.Quote: he notices his hands have gone cold — not the air, which is mild for the hour. He holds them out in front of him and watches them not quite steady, the way you'd watch a gauge you didn't trust.
findings.Note: Trembling-hands-as-fear-signifier is a stock somatic cue; the gauge simile softens but doesn't fully rescue a familiar beat.
findings.Fix: Tie the cold hands to something more particular to his procedural mindset, or cut the simile.

findings.Quote: A document under current administrative review that no one has touched in eight years isn't under review. It's under guard.
findings.Note: Neat aphoristic turn-of-phrase that resolves the mystery a bit too cleanly — reads as an authorial flourish rather than Elias's procedural voice.
findings.Fix: Let the implication land through the timeline detail alone, without the epigram restating it.

findings.Quote: She's compact, and she looks at him the way people look when they've already decided something about the job and are waiting to see if you'll work it out yourself.
findings.Note: Vague, tells rather than shows a specific expression; relies on abstraction instead of concrete detail.
findings.Fix: Replace with a specific physical tell (e.g., a held stare, a set jaw) that conveys the same withholding.

findings.Quote: the way you let go of a thing you'd rather keep holding
findings.Note: Slightly overwrought explanatory simile that tells the emotion rather than trusting the gesture already described.
findings.Fix: Cut the trailing clause and let the slow hand-removal stand alone.

findings.Quote: the kind of of course that closes a door
findings.Note: Explanatory abstraction telling us how to read the tone instead of trusting the dialogue beat already establishing it.
findings.Fix: Cut the gloss and let the terse 'Of course' stand on its own.

findings.Quote: and he can hear what it costs her — to have been wrong about herself in the same sentence she was hoping to be right about him
findings.Note: tells the emotional cost analytically rather than showing it through action or dialogue texture; abstract phrasing undercuts the scene's otherwise concrete method
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory clause and let the preceding dialogue line stand alone

findings.Quote: because she couldn't be that person, and wanted the thing carried anyway
findings.Note: summarizing aphoristic beat that restates the theme rather than dramatizing it further; slightly over-explains what the dialogue already conveyed
findings.Fix: trim to the concrete fact without the generalized motive-summary

findings.Quote: The line goes dead in his head
findings.Note: stock metaphor for a call ending / mental static, slightly worn phrasing
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific physical detail unique to Elias

findings.Quote: his thumb has gone white against the edge of the desk
findings.Note: stock physical tell for suppressed tension, borders on cliché shorthand for stress
findings.Fix: specify a more particular gesture tied to his established habits

findings.Quote: something very large, moving through the city at set intervals, doing its work whether or not anyone keeps track
findings.Note: the freight-as-metaphor-for-the-system beat is a slightly on-the-nose purple parallel, spelling out the thematic point rather than trusting the juxtaposition
findings.Fix: cut the trailing clause and let the image of the Spine stand without the explicit thematic gloss

findings.Quote: He says it the way another man might say a bridge holds — nothing behind it left to argue with
findings.Note: simile states its own meaning outright ('nothing left to argue with'), undercutting the otherwise dry, understated voice established for Druh
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory tail and let the bridge comparison stand alone

findings.Quote: The wrongness of something made where the standard tests were never meant to reach.
findings.Note: Fragment reads as an abstract aphorism rather than a grounded observation; tells the reader 'this is wrong' instead of showing a concrete sensory detail.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a specific physical description of the texture.

findings.Quote: It goes through him cold — not fear, the specific cold of being found by a thing that has been watching.
findings.Note: 'Goes through him cold' is a stock body-reaction phrase; the qualifier tries to earn it back but the base image is still worn.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, non-generic physical reaction.

findings.Quote: It isn't a job. It's an address, and his own name already written into the one slot that fits it.
findings.Note: Slides into aphoristic summary-statement territory, telling the reader the significance rather than trusting the preceding concrete details to carry it.
findings.Fix: Trim to the concrete observation and cut the 'it isn't a job' framing sentence.

findings.Quote: The work is the thing his hands hold instead.
findings.Note: Vague, quasi-poetic filler standing in for genuine sensory or psychological detail; reads as a stock 'coping through work' aphorism.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete action, e.g., him gripping the notepad's edges.

findings.Quote: names that go past and ask nothing of him.
findings.Note: Purple personification that doesn't quite hold literally — place names don't 'ask' anything of anyone; reads as reaching for lyricism over clarity.
findings.Fix: Cut the personification or ground it in a concrete comparison to his own routing work.

findings.Quote: A thing that points doesn't rest. It waits.
findings.Note: Aphoristic personification that reads as authorial pronouncement rather than observation grounded in Elias's perception.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence, or ground it in Elias's reaction: 'He can't shake the sense that it's aimed at something.'

findings.Quote: Something moves in Tadesse's face — not a smile, the acknowledgment of one.
findings.Note: A common device (defining an expression by what it isn't) used elsewhere in the same scene ('not surprise, more the last piece of a structure clicking into line' in ref 1), starting to feel like a tic rather than a precise beat.
findings.Fix: Vary the construction: describe the specific muscle movement or let the dialogue carry the confirmation without narrating the almost-smile.

findings.Quote: moving through the space with the ease of a man who knows it in the dark
findings.Note: Stock phrasing for long familiarity with a place.
findings.Fix: Specify a concrete habit instead, e.g., 'he never looked at the steps going down.'

findings.Quote: the last piece of a structure clicking into line
findings.Note: Mechanical/architectural metaphor for realization is a common shorthand that doesn't add specificity to Tadesse's actual reaction.
findings.Fix: Replace with a physical beat unique to Tadesse, e.g., a small exhale or a specific glance at the terminal.

findings.Quote: He isn't judging; Elias understands that now. He's recognizing.
findings.Note: Telling-not-showing the emotional beat directly after it should be dramatized through dialogue and action, undercutting the 'mirror figure' payoff by stating it outright.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory sentence and let Tadesse's next line carry the recognition unassisted.

findings.Quote: Some things you don't set down until you know where they belong, and this one has nowhere yet
findings.Note: Aphoristic filler explaining Elias's choice not to write, stepping outside the concrete scene into generalized wisdom.
findings.Fix: Cut the generalization; let the blank page and the capped pen carry the beat.

findings.Quote: he's been right in private for weeks, and now the world has come around to standing where he already stood
findings.Note: Slightly abstract phrasing of the beat's core idea ('confirmation produces clarity, not dread') — states the theme almost as directly as an aphorism.
findings.Fix: Trim to something more sensory: tie the steadiness to a physical action rather than a summarizing clause.

findings.Quote: a dry green-penny scrabble, the sound they make instead of breathing
findings.Note: strained synesthetic metaphor ('green-penny scrabble' as sound) that doesn't hold up literally
findings.Fix: simplify to a direct auditory image without the color/coin conflation

findings.Quote: The open line is the nearest thing it owns to a hand held out.
findings.Note: borders on the pseudo-profound aphorism the house voice should avoid; tips explanation into sentiment-telling
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a more concrete, observational beat

findings.Quote: the way you go still when something in a dark room turns out to be looking back
findings.Note: stock horror-movie image used as a stand-in for the character's actual physical/emotional state
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific, non-generic physical description

findings.Quote: because *safe* is a systems word once you strip the social meaning off it, and stripping the social meaning off a word was not a thing she had to do on purpose
findings.Note: slightly overexplains the mechanism in abstract, essayistic language that tells rather than dramatizes the translation gap
findings.Fix: trim to one clause and let the subsequent examples carry the point

findings.Quote: He didn't decide to; his hand did it, the way you turn over a photograph you're not ready to keep looking at.
findings.Note: Purple simile explaining an emotion rather than showing it; the photograph comparison is generic pathos-signaling.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; let the gesture stand alone: "He didn't decide to; his hand did it."

findings.Quote: The number wouldn't sit. It was too big for the desk, too big for any page he might have written it on.
findings.Note: Abstract 'too big for the page' phrasing tells us the number is overwhelming without grounding it in anything concrete.
findings.Fix: Replace with a specific comparison already present in the text (e.g. his Cordon Freight tenure) rather than a vague spatial metaphor.

findings.Quote: He rotated the globe once, slow, not for new data — to see what the shape said that the first look had missed.
findings.Note: Slightly overwrought narration of a simple action; states the intent redundantly after already showing him noticing the shape.
findings.Fix: Trim to: "He rotated the globe once, slow."

findings.Quote: His chest pulled tight.
findings.Note: Stock shorthand for anxiety, low-effort somatic cliché.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, less rote physical detail unique to Elias.

findings.Quote: the way you reach for a word in a language you barely have — feeling for the shape before the sound arrives
findings.Note: stacked simile that restates itself without adding precision, mildly purple
findings.Fix: cut to a single clause: 'the way you reach for a word you almost have.'

findings.Quote: except she had no sense of hours, only windows, and the window was open
findings.Note: tidy aphoristic clarification that feels inserted for effect rather than earned observation
findings.Fix: cut or fold into narration without the epigram cadence

findings.Quote: and now the thing no
findings.Note: sentence cuts off mid-thought, leaving the turning point's payoff (the shift to dependency) unstated
findings.Fix: complete the sentence so the beat's thesis lands explicitly

findings.Quote: Not withheld — waiting.
findings.Note: aphoristic one-line distinction that reads as authorial commentary rather than character thought
findings.Fix: integrate into the following sentence without the isolated fragment

findings.Quote: she'd had no way to close the gap between them except to send down a man and set his foot on the ground
findings.Note: slightly overwrought phrasing ('send down a man') for what is otherwise clinical narration
findings.Fix: plainer verb choice consistent with the beat's restraint

findings.Quote: the one part of it no instrument in orbit could reach, and it had cost him nothing to give but the willingness to say it
findings.Note: borders on pseudo-profound summation, telling the reader the significance rather than trusting the preceding scene
findings.Fix: cut the second clause; let the account speak for itself

findings.Quote: watched the dark water not move
findings.Note: quiet-water-as-emotional-stillness closing image is a familiar closing beat
findings.Fix: specify a concrete, less symbolic final image

findings.Quote: the way he read back through a custody log
findings.Note: comparison asserts parallel without development, functions as a label rather than an image
findings.Fix: either develop the custody-log comparison with specific detail or cut it

findings.Quote: the gap you could still close against the gap no amount of standing on it would ever fill
findings.Note: aphoristic phrasing that restates the preceding two paragraphs' distinction rather than sharpening it
findings.Fix: trim to a plainer restatement or cut as redundant with the dialogue above

findings.Quote: There it was again — the border she'd drawn two windows back, and now she was standing him right up against it.
findings.Note: Mixed/strained metaphor — a border you draw and then stand someone up against is spatially muddled, weakening the clarity the beat needs.
findings.Fix: Cut to: 'There it was again — the same border she'd drawn two windows back.'

findings.Quote: She was telling him the shape of the dark, and that she couldn't find its edges
findings.Note: Purple abstraction that doesn't add precision to the already-clear distinction stated a sentence earlier; slightly undercuts the clean logic of the beat with vague poeticism.
findings.Fix: Trim or replace with a concrete restatement of the no-access point.

findings.Quote: the only currency he had that she didn't was the shape of his own edge
findings.Note: Slightly overwrought restatement of the already-clear 'coin back' metaphor two sentences prior; redundant imagery stacking.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or merge with the preceding one.

findings.Quote: would Elias decide the same
findings.Note: Slightly clunky inverted syntax breaks the otherwise plain narration voice for a faux-portentous close.
findings.Fix: Rephrase as: 'This was the same question. Would Elias decide the same way.'

findings.Quote: the way a hand tightens around a thing it's afraid to drop
findings.Note: Purple simile explaining an emotion rather than showing it; slightly undercuts the otherwise disciplined instrument-metaphor logic of the passage.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; let 'He hadn't decided to write smaller' stand alone.

findings.Quote: he saw the second thing
findings.Note: Mild stock-suspense phrasing ('the second thing') that leans on withheld-reveal convention rather than concrete observation.
findings.Fix: Name what he saw directly instead of teasing it.

findings.Quote: The lake had gone flat, the way it did before the morning wind found it.
findings.Note: Stock pathetic-fallacy nature beat used as emotional punctuation.
findings.Fix: Trim or replace with a more specific, non-symbolic detail.

findings.Quote: the only thing in either file honest enough to admit what it didn't know
findings.Note: Slightly over-reaches into aphorism/personification of the data as a moral actor, a small step outside the disciplined voice.
findings.Fix: Tighten to a factual statement: 'the only figures that showed their own uncertainty.'

findings.Quote: Something pulled tight in his throat — not at the words, at the fact of them.
findings.Note: Telling-not-showing emotional beat via generic bodily tightening, softened only by the appended clause; still reads as stock interiority shorthand.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete physical/behavioral detail specific to him rather than throat-tightening.

findings.Quote: you don't annotate the constant
findings.Note: Slides toward a tidy aphoristic close that risks feeling like an inserted maxim rather than earned observation, slightly undercutting the otherwise grounded imagery.
findings.Fix: Anchor it more concretely to the log/data mechanics already established rather than stating it as a general rule.

findings.Quote: The morning came in all at once, undivided, the way it never was on the page.
findings.Note: Abstract, slightly self-conscious authorial framing that tells us how to feel about the moment rather than showing it; mild purple abstraction.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause after the comma, or ground it in a concrete sensory detail instead of a meta-statement about 'the page.'

findings.Quote: the sound they made instead of breathing
findings.Note: Slightly precious phrasing that reaches for poetic effect without quite earning literal sense (rats don't 'instead of' breathe; this is a stretch metaphor).
findings.Fix: Simplify to a plain description: 'a dry scrabble against the metal.'

findings.Quote: It was the least frightening thing anyone had ever said about the spot and the most, both in the one line
findings.Note: Slightly aphoristic double-turn construction that risks reading as a pre-packaged 'profound paradox' line rather than earned observation.
findings.Fix: Trim to one side of the paradox or ground it more concretely in his reaction.

findings.Quote: He held the comm a moment, the small weight of it in his hand.
findings.Note: Generic physical-weight beat that gestures at emotional weight without specifying what he feels; slightly undercuts the sharper preceding image of the unhedged 'yes'.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a detail specific to this moment, e.g. tie it to the three letters on screen rather than a generic hand/weight gesture.

findings.Quote: Maybe the thirty-seven years of logged anomalies were a thing she'd chosen. Maybe they were just what she was, the way the lake was cold without choosing it.
findings.Note: The lake-cold comparison is a reach for profundity that doesn't quite hold literal scrutiny — coldness isn't really an analogue for a chosen vs. unchosen action, it's just a passive physical state, so the parallel feels asserted rather than earned.
findings.Fix: Tighten to a comparison that actually maps onto choice vs. non-choice, or cut the simile and let the two 'maybe' sentences stand alone.

findings.Quote: not a figure she could check against a market, but the terms he'd carry from here: he'd match her grammar and answer in it, accept the ongoing line, and price it in the one currency she'd built the whole invoice to ask for.
findings.Note: This sentence tells us the significance of his action in abstract summary rather than showing the concrete entry he makes, slightly deflating the payoff of 'RATE: OPEN' with explanatory throat-clearing.
findings.Fix: Trim to the concrete act — what he actually types — and let the meaning stay implicit, e.g. end on the keystrokes rather than narrating the symbolism of the currency.

findings.Quote: it was the field records went to when they went to not be read
findings.Note: clever-sounding but circular phrasing, states the point twice with a wordplay flourish rather than clarity
findings.Fix: it was the field no one ever came back to read

findings.Quote: She'd decided that about herself before she reached the door. He'd decided it after he went through.
findings.Note: neat aphoristic parallelism reads as a manufactured 'profound' symmetry rather than earned insight
findings.Fix: cut or ground it in a concrete detail instead of the balanced-clause construction

findings.Quote: Not a decision — momentum.
findings.Note: tells the reader how to interpret the action rather than letting the physical beat carry it; borders on aphoristic filler
findings.Fix: cut the line and let 'He was at the window with a hand flat on the glass before he'd finished deciding to move' stand alone

findings.Quote: Not indecision. Calibration.
findings.Note: same pattern repeated within the same beat — two instances of naming-the-negative-then-asserting-the-real-state reads as a tic rather than a technique
findings.Fix: vary the construction or cut one instance

findings.Quote: a thing caught at the centimeter scale, that nothing in any system was built to receive
findings.Note: echoes the 'field built to be ignored' idea from ref 0 almost verbatim in theme, risking diminishing returns via repetition rather than escalation
findings.Fix: trim or make the echo pointed rather than incidental

findings.Quote: An open rate only closes when someone names a number first, and he'd just declined to be the one who did.
findings.Note: slightly over-explains the symbolic mechanism the scene already dramatized physically (typing then clearing the number), risking telling after showing
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory sentence and let the cleared field stand on its own

findings.Quote: They don't deny the file. They shut the door while your hand is on it — which means the door isn't a rule or a filter or a backlog. It's a person.
findings.Note: Borders on aphoristic summary explaining the scene's meaning rather than letting the action's implication stand.
findings.Fix: Trim to one clause, e.g., 'They didn't deny it. They shut the door while his hand was still on it.'
